tagline: Loop roads through the dark cotton soil and its long memory.
intro: The Black Belt takes its name from the soil, rich and black, that grew the region's cotton in the 19th century. The trail is not one road but a set of loops across 13 counties, out of Livingston and Aliceville, Demopolis and Marion, Selma and Camden, Tuskegee and Union Springs, through country the Black Warrior, Tombigbee and Alabama rivers have shaped as they wander.
More than 50 stops lie along them, from Ezell's Fish Camp and its fried catfish to the old temple complex at Moundville and the mansions of Demopolis and Greensboro.

moments.title: Gaineswood
moments.text: Begun in 1843 as a log dog-trot cabin and grown over eighteen years into a Greek Revival mansion, much of the work done by enslaved people, finished on the eve of the Civil War.

moments.title: Edmund Pettus Bridge
moments.text: On March 7, 1965, Bloody Sunday, police attacked voting rights marchers here as they set out for Montgomery, and on March 21 the marchers crossed again and walked on to the Capitol.

moments.title: Lowndesboro
moments.text: A planters' town once called McGill's Hill, its churches along one county road run from 1830 to 1888, and the oldest wears the dome from Alabama's first capitol at Cahawba, now a ghost town.
